_readme: Colour code: [[c:...]] CYAN = not confirmed yet (a best guess or a new idea from Claude, for the owner to approve). Plain text = confirmed by the owner.
name: Former Wesleyan chapel

layers.essential_history: It has a red-brick front, a round window and a Wesleyan stone. [[c:The village board says it replaced a smaller chapel in Church Street. It's a private home now. An earlier note gives 1808 for the smaller chapel, but we haven't checked that.]]
layers.deeper_history: [[c:There's more history for this stop to come.]]
layers.mystery: [[c:Journal page: ]]Alice[[c: came back from the dispatch room the long way round, and she hasn't said why. The chapel you can see today is much newer than our story, which is set in the 1600s, but it's here to unlock this page.]]

puzzle.title: The stone
puzzle.intro: [[c:Stand on the public road and look at the front of the building. Please don't go through any gate.]]
puzzle.question: [[c:What year is shown on the chapel's stone?]]
hints: [[c:Look for a stone set into the red brick.]]
[[c:It's a four-digit year, on the stone that mentions the Wesleyans.]]
puzzle.fallback: [[c:Can't read the stone? Look at the photo at the top of this page.]]

directions_to_next: [[c:Head on to the Old Bakehouse, just a little further along. Full directions coming soon.]]
private_note: This is a private home, so please look from the road only.
notes: Never present the 1881 building as existing in the 1600s.

sources.title: Village history board (photos taken on the recce, 19 Oct 2026)
